title: Introduction to PHP
objectives: Explain the purpose of PHP.

introduction: Variables and Constants develops $ variables; naming; assignment; reassignment; case sensitivity; define(); const. Apply these ideas to student information and core PHP web development.
explanation:
Key concepts: $ variables; naming; assignment; reassignment; case sensitivity; define(); const.

Variables begin with $, followed by a letter or underscore and then letters, digits, or underscores. $name and $Name are different variables. Assignment uses = and can replace a value. introduction: Conditional Statements develops if; else; elseif; switch; nested conditions; logical comparisons. Apply these ideas to student information and core PHP web development.
explanation:
Key concepts: if; else; elseif; switch; nested conditions; logical comparisons.

Conditions select a branch. Check the most restrictive grade range first so 95 is not caught by a lower threshold. elseif belongs to the same decision chain; nested conditions add a decision inside another. switch compares cases and typically needs break to prevent fall-through. Reject grades outside 0–100 before classifying them.
syntax:
<?php
$grade = 88;
if ($grade < 0 || $grade > 100) { echo "Invalid grade"; }
elseif ($grade >= 90) { echo "Excellent"; }
elseif ($grade >= 85) { echo "Very Good"; }
elseif ($grade >= 80) { echo "Good"; }
elseif ($grade >= 75) { echo "Passed"; }
else { echo "Failed"; }

introduction: Functions develops declaration; calls; parameters; return; defaults; local/global scope. Apply these ideas to student information and core PHP web development.
explanation:
Key concepts: declaration; calls; parameters; return; defaults; local/global scope.

Functions package reusable behavior. Parameters pass values into local scope and return sends a result to the caller. A default argument makes a parameter optional. Local variables are not the same as globals; passing dependencies explicitly makes a function easier to test than using global. A declared return type documents and enforces the contract.
syntax:
<?php
function average(array $grades): float {
    if (count($grades) === 0) { throw new InvalidArgumentException("At least one grade is required."); }
    return array_sum($grades) / count($grades);
}
function result(float $grade, float $threshold = 75): string {
    return $grade >= $threshold ? "PASSED" : "FAILED";
}
echo number_format(average([85, 90, 90.5]), 2) . " | " . result(88.5);

explanation:
Key concepts: public/private/protected; getters/setters; interfaces; implements; traits/use.

Encapsulation controls access to state: public is externally accessible; protected is available to the class and descendants; private belongs to its declaring class. A getter reads state and a validated setter changes it. Interfaces define method contracts that implementing classes must fulfill. Traits reuse method implementations without a parent-child relationship.
syntax:
<?php
interface Describable { public function describe(): string; }
trait Greeting { public function greet(): string { return "Hello"; } }
class Student implements Describable {
    use Greeting;
    private string $name = "Maria";
    public function describe(): string { return $this->greet() . " " . $this->name; }
}
echo (new Student())->describe();

activity:
PHP Student Information Web Application
Functional requirements: registration, login/logout, dashboard, Admin/Staff/Student permissions, student CRUD, MySQL, search/filtering, form validation, PDO parameters, password_hash/password_verify, regenerated sessions, profile images, CSRF tokens, escaping, and friendly errors. Optional modules: Courses, Subjects, Users, Reports.
Database design: users(id, email unique, password VARCHAR(255), role); students(id, user_id foreign key, student_number unique, first_name, last_name, course, year_level, email, profile_image). Add courses/subjects and junction tables if needed.
Milestones: 1. Design schema and role/ownership matrix. 2. Build MVC-style folders/config. 3. Implement registration/login/logout securely. 4. Add validated CRUD/search/filtering. 5. Add controlled images and CSRF. 6. Test every role and ownership boundary. 7. Document installation with placeholder configuration.
Security checklist: prepared SQL; escaped output; CSRF on writes; hashed passwords; regenerated session IDs; HTTPS cookie flags; upload MIME/size limits and non-executable storage; private errors; environment secrets; least privilege.
Testing checklist: duplicate registration, wrong password, expired session, denied roles, another student ID, SQL/XSS payloads, missing/wrong CSRF, invalid forms, oversized/fake images, search/filtering, rollback, and logout.
Submit a PHP entry script plus schema, folder map, milestones, test matrix, and optional educational repository URL in comments. Full multi-page/MySQL execution requires a teacher-provisioned sandbox outside CodeLab; the lab practices isolated components.
